mathcounts-potw-2026-03-09-01.title: Step by step
mathcounts-potw-2026-03-09-01.body:
$\frac23$ of $\frac12$ is $\frac13$ of the pie; $\frac14$ of $\frac13$ is $\frac{1}{12}$.

**Answer: $\frac{1}{12}$**

mathcounts-potw-2026-03-09-02.title: Fraction of the circle
mathcounts-potw-2026-03-09-02.body:
The slice is $\frac{20}{360} = \frac{1}{18}$ of the pie, so its arc is $\frac{1}{18}$ of the circumference: $C = 18 \times \pi = 18\pi$.

**Answer: $18\pi$**

mathcounts-potw-2026-03-09-03.title: Arc plus two radii
mathcounts-potw-2026-03-09-03.body:
The slice is $\frac{20}{360} = \frac1{18}$ of the pie, so the full circumference is $18\pi$ and the radius is $r = 18\pi \div 2\pi = 9$.
The remaining piece is bounded by the remaining arc, $18\pi - \pi = 17\pi$, and two radii (the cuts), $2 \times 9 = 18$. Perimeter: $18 + 17\pi$.

**Answer: $18 + 17\pi$ units**

mathcounts-potw-2026-03-09-03.title: Using the remaining angle
mathcounts-potw-2026-03-09-03.body:
The remaining sector has angle $340°$. From $\frac{20}{360}(2\pi r) = \pi$ we get $r = 9$. Arc $= \frac{340}{360} \cdot 18\pi = 17\pi$; add the two radii: $17\pi + 18$.

**Answer: $18 + 17\pi$ units**
